game.answer: Fall by about 191 milligals: g(r) = g₀·r/R, so the change is g₀ × 1,240 ÷ 6,371,000. The measurement is a rise of 105, so the earth is not uniform.

derive.goal: the predicted change in g over the depth of the shaft, in milligals
derive.startNote: R = 6,371 km, g₀ = 9.812 m/s² at the surface; the inset is 1,240 m below it

steps.ask: Say which mass acts at a radius inside the sphere.

candidates.text: the whole mass of the sphere, wherever you are inside it
the mass of the shells above the radius
no mass at all, since the pulls cancel
the mass of the sphere below the radius

steps.ask: Write that mass in terms of the density.
Put it into the inverse-square law.

candidates.text: g(r) = (4/3)πGρ·r², so gravity falls as the square of the radius
g(r) = (4/3)πGρ/r, so gravity grows towards the centre
g(r) = (4/3)πGρ·r, so gravity is proportional to the radius
g(r) = GρV/r², with V the whole volume

steps.ask: Evaluate the change over the depth of the shaft.

candidates.text: Δg = g₀·(d/R)² = 3.7 × 10⁻⁸ m/s², which is nothing at all
Δg = −g₀·d/R = −1.91 × 10⁻³ m/s², a fall of 191 milligals
Δg = −g₀·d/R = −1.91 × 10⁻³ m/s², a fall of 1.91 milligals

derive.hint: Each line has to follow from the one above it, and each one is licensed by a rule.

assumes: a spherical shell of matter exerts no net pull on anything inside it
newton's law of gravitation — taken as read

equations.e: g(r) = GMr/R³ inside,  g = GM/r² outside
equations.c: gravity inside and outside a uniform sphere
v: the gravitational constant, 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ in SI units
the mass of the whole sphere, in kilograms
how far from the centre the measurement is made
equations.s: Outside a sphere the whole mass acts as though it were at the centre; inside one, the shells above you contribute nothing and only the mass below counts.

concept.c: The field inside a uniform sphere, and the shell theorem
concept.t: Matter arranged in a shell around you pulls you nowhere, so inside a sphere only the mass below counts and gravity grows in proportion to the radius. It is what makes a measurement of gravity underground a measurement of the rock above it.
rests: Newton's law of gravitation

GRAV.title: Two thousand six hundred and seventy
GRAV.takeaway: A gravity gradient down a shaft constrains the density of the rock passed through, and constrains nothing about what is deeper.
